title: Saying “People in General”: man, en, du, and folk
goal: Choose the right Norwegian generic pronoun for grammar, tone, and sentence role.

objectives.statement: Choose the right Norwegian generic pronoun for grammar, tone, and sentence role.

spans.value: Nora and Elias work at a tourist office near a popular mountain trail. They are revising safety information for visitors. The facts are clear, but they disagree about how the advice should sound.
Her står det: Når man går i fjellet, må man være forberedt på raske værskifter.

blocks.translation: It says here: When you go hiking in the mountains, you must be prepared for sudden changes in the weather.

spans.value: Det er korrekt, men litt formelt. Kan vi skrive: Når du går i fjellet, må du være forberedt?

blocks.translation: That is correct, but a little formal. Can we write: When you go hiking in the mountains, you must be prepared?

spans.value: Ja, det høres mer direkte ut. Men noen lesere kan tro at vi snakker til dem personlig.

blocks.translation: Yes, that sounds more direct. But some readers may think that we are speaking to them personally.

spans.value: Det er kanskje meningen. Vi gir jo råd til den som leser.

blocks.translation: Perhaps that is the point. We are giving advice to whoever is reading.

spans.value: Sant. Lenger nede står det at dårlig vær kan gjøre man usikker. Det er vel feil?

blocks.translation: True. Farther down it says that bad weather can make one uncertain. That is wrong, isn’t it?

spans.value: Ja. I en upersonlig man/en-referanse kan man bruke «man» som subjekt, men ikke som objekt. Vi må skrive at dårlig vær kan gjøre en usikker.

blocks.translation: Yes. Within an impersonal man/en reference, man can be used as the subject, but not as the object. We must write that bad weather can make one uncertain.

spans.value: Og hva med denne setningen: Folk glemmer ofte at det blir kaldere om kvelden?

blocks.translation: And what about this sentence: People often forget that it gets colder in the evening?

spans.value: Den passer hvis vi mener at mange besøkende faktisk gjør det. Man glemmer ofte høres mer ut som en generell menneskelig tendens.

blocks.translation: That works if we mean that many visitors actually do it. Man glemmer ofte sounds more like a general human tendency.

spans.value: Nora keeps all four expressions, but she uses them in different parts of the information sheet. The choice is not only about grammar. It also changes the tone and the kind of generalization being made.

sections.title: What are Nora and Elias trying to say?

spans.value: Norwegian has several ways to refer to people in general without naming one particular person:

items.value: presents something as generally true of any person in the situation.

addresses the reader or listener directly but can still mean anyone in that situation.
means people as a group, often a real or imaginable group rather than an abstract individual.

spans.value: Are you describing what any person typically does, involving the listener directly, or talking about people as a group—and what grammatical role does the expression have?
is common when stating a general rule, experience, expectation, or human tendency. Grammatically, it functions as a subject.

no.value: Man lærer mye av å gjøre feil.

en.value: You learn a lot from making mistakes.

no.value: Man må ha billett for å ta toget.

en.value: You need a ticket to take the train.

no.value: I Norge tar man ofte av seg skoene når man kommer inn.

en.value: In Norway, people often take off their shoes when they come inside.

spans.value: with generic you, people, one, or a passive construction. Do not expect one fixed English equivalent.

no.value: Her kan man kjøpe mat hele døgnet.

en.value: Food can be bought here around the clock.

spans.value: The Norwegian sentence literally presents a general person who can buy food. Natural English may instead use a passive form.
refers broadly to people, it is grammatically singular:

no.value: Man må ta ansvar for det man gjør.

en.value: One must take responsibility for what one does.

no.value: Hvis man bestiller tidlig, får man som regel en bedre pris.

en.value: If you book early, you usually get a better price.

spans.value: The speaker is not necessarily advising one specific listener. The sentence describes a general consequence.

spans.value: This is the grammatical problem Nora notices in the draft.

no.value: Dårlig vær kan gjøre en usikker.

en.value: Bad weather can make you uncertain.

en.value: Comments like that can make one nervous.

no.value: Ingen liker å bli behandlet som om en ikke forstår noe.

en.value: No one likes to be treated as though one does not understand anything.

en.value: You easily become tired in intense heat.

sections.title: Recognition note: referring back to the same generic person

spans.value: in the examples below refers back to the generic subject.

no.value: Man må beskytte seg mot sola.

en.value: You have to protect yourself from the sun.

no.value: En bør spørre seg om turen passer for alle.

en.value: One should ask oneself whether the trip is suitable for everyone.

spans.value: The possessive forms in the following examples also refer back to the generic subject; choosing among those forms is outside this lesson’s objective.

no.value: Man må kjenne sine egne grenser.

en.value: You have to know your own limits.

no.value: En bør ta med seg maten sin.

en.value: One should bring one’s food along.

spans.value: These forms are reference cues only. They do not turn
into an object and are not assessed here.

no.value: Man må ta vare på seg selv.

en.value: One must take care of oneself.

no.value: Andre kan hjelpe en.

en.value: Other people can help one.

spans.value: These reference forms remain supporting context only; no reflexive or possessive choice is requested or scored.
is grammatically the ordinary second-person pronoun, but it does not always refer only to one specific listener. It can mean anyone who finds themself in the described situation.

no.value: Når du flytter til et nytt sted, tar det tid å bli kjent med folk.

en.value: When you move to a new place, it takes time to get to know people.

spans.value: The speaker is not necessarily claiming that the listener is moving. The sentence invites the listener to imagine the general experience.
is especially common in conversation, advice, instructions, and accessible public information.

no.value: Hvis du tar bussen etter midnatt, må du kjøpe billetten på forhånd.

en.value: If you take the bus after midnight, you have to buy the ticket in advance.

no.value: Hvis man tar bussen etter midnatt, må man kjøpe billetten på forhånd.

en.value: If one takes the bus after midnight, one must buy the ticket in advance.

no.value: Hvis du tar bussen etter midnatt, må du kjøpe billetten på forhånd.

en.value: If you take the bus after midnight, you have to buy the ticket in advance.

spans.value: version presents a neutral general rule. The
version turns toward the reader and makes the advice feel more immediate.
is always friendlier. In criticism or discussion of sensitive behavior, generic
may sound as though the speaker is accusing the actual listener.

no.value: Du blir fort irritert når du ikke får det som du vil.

en.value: You quickly become irritated when you do not get what you want.

spans.value: Even if the speaker intends a general observation, the listener may hear a personal judgment.

no.value: Man blir fort irritert når man ikke får det som man vil.

en.value: People quickly become irritated when they do not get what they want.

spans.value: The choice therefore depends on communicative distance. Use
when involving the addressee is useful. Use
when the statement should remain detached from the particular listener.

sections.title: Folk for people as a group

spans.value: is a noun meaning people. It commonly refers to a group, category, or population rather than to an abstract representative person.

no.value: Folk spør ofte hvor lang turen er.

en.value: People often ask how long the hike is.

no.value: Mange folk undervurderer hvor raskt været kan skifte.

en.value: Many people underestimate how quickly the weather can change.

no.value: Vi prøver å gi folk tydelig informasjon.

en.value: We try to give people clear information.

spans.value: can be either subject or object without changing form:

no.value: Folk trenger tydelige råd.

en.value: People need clear advice.

no.value: Tydelige råd hjelper folk.

en.value: Clear advice helps people.

spans.value: The meaning also differs slightly from

no.value: Man glemmer lett tiden når man har det hyggelig.

en.value: You easily lose track of time when you are enjoying yourself.

no.value: Folk glemmer ofte tiden på denne kafeen.

en.value: People often lose track of time in this café.

spans.value: The first sounds like a general human tendency. The second suggests an observed pattern among actual café customers.

no.value: Man bruker mindre strøm hvis man senker temperaturen.

en.value: You use less electricity if you lower the temperature.

no.value: Folk bruker mindre strøm enn før.

en.value: People use less electricity than before.

spans.value: sentence describes what happens to any person under a condition. The
sentence makes a claim about people collectively.
is simply a more informal substitute for
. It changes the perspective from a representative individual to a group.

en.value: When you go hiking in the mountains, you must be prepared for sudden changes in the weather. Bring clothes that protect you from wind and rain.

en.value: One should always check the weather forecast before leaving. Bad weather can make one uncertain, and one must know one’s own limits.

en.value: People often ask whether they can do the hike without a map.

sections.title: Cumulative transfer: advice at a public swimming pool

spans.value: Move to a new everyday situation. A swimming pool needs three kinds of text: direct guidance for visitors, a neutral explanation of general safety, and a staff note about behavior observed among customers.
Without returning to the explanation, the learner should briefly state when
are appropriate, then apply each form in a new everyday sentence.

prompt.value: Examine statements from the visitor information and select the one that describes any person in the situation, not a named or specific individual. Sentence role and tone are context only, not scoring targets.

options.why: The statement refers to the named individual Nora.

options.text: Elias snakker med en bestemt besøkende om sikkerhet.
options.why: The statement refers to Elias and one specific visitor.

options.text: Når man besøker fjellene, bør man sjekke værmeldingen.
options.why: Man refers to any person in a general rule or consequence.

stem.value: Choose the statement that uses man as a generic subject.

prompt.value: Complete each mountain-safety sentence. Use the specified impersonal man/en reference: both forms are possible in generic-subject slots, but only en is possible in an object slot. Tone is context, not scored.

explanation.value: «man» and «en» can both be generic subjects, but only «en» can be the object. «folk» presents people as an observed group rather than one representative person.

spans.value: være forberedt på raskt værskifte. Dårlig vær kan overraske

prompt.value: Write two short Norwegian tourist-office messages about checking the weather before mountain travel. Give the same information twice: first as direct visitor guidance, then as a neutral report about safe travel. Change the generic subject while keeping its sentence position constant in both messages.

payload.judge_prompt: Check both messages against the task and report evidence for each criterion.

criteria.instruction: Uses du for deliberate reader involvement in the first message.
Uses man for detached generalization in the second message.
Keeps the underlying information the same and keeps the generic subject in the same sentence position in both messages.

prompt.value: Classify each observation by meaning: representative individual generalization or behavior observed among visitors as a group. Use meaning, not formality, as the deciding factor.

items.text: Når man arbeider på turistkontoret, får man mange spørsmål.
Folk spør ofte om værmeldingen før fjellturen.
Når man hjelper besøkende, må man lytte nøye.
Folk venter ved skranken når det begynner å regne.

prompt.value: Write three short Norwegian statements for a public swimming pool: direct guidance for visitors, a neutral explanation of general safety, and a staff note about behavior observed among customers. Across the statements, use all four forms man, en, du, and folk according to meaning, tone, and sentence role. Include at least one generic person in a non-subject role. Keep swimming-pool vocabulary incidental; it is not being assessed.

payload.judge_prompt: Check the three statements against the task and report evidence for each criterion. Score pronoun choices, meanings, tones, and sentence roles; do not score swimming vocabulary beyond whether it remains incidental.

criteria.instruction: Uses man for detached generalization, en in an appropriate non-subject role within the impersonal man/en reference, du for direct visitor involvement, and folk for a collective group.
Includes at least one generic person in a non-subject role.
Keeps swimming-pool vocabulary incidental rather than making it the scored evidence.

prompt.value: Write a brief Norwegian rule summary and four new everyday sentences. In the summary, state the distinctions among the impersonal man/en pair, direct du and non-subject deg, and collective folk. Then apply each distinction in a new sentence, using each target form in an appropriate grammatical role.

payload.judge_prompt: Check the rule summary and four new everyday sentences against the task and report evidence for each criterion.

criteria.instruction: States that man is subject-only and en is the object form within an impersonal man/en reference, and applies this distinction in a new sentence.
States that du is used for direct listener involvement and uses deg outside subject position in a new sentence.
States that folk refers to a collective and uses folk unchanged as an object in a new sentence.
